To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
thermally induced birefingence in Nd-doped YAG ceramic rods is caused by the difference between the thermal expansion coefficients of the dopant and host material.
the birefringent properties of Nd:YAG polycrystalls are determined by the grain size and that these properties may be compensated for by use of known methods.
thermally induced birefingence in polycrystals is the main reason of depolarization of the laser radiation and that the modulation depth is determined by the grain length.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the influence of thermal birefringences on the properties of Nd:YAG laser rods.
the investigation of laser ceramics and their application in solid-state lasers.
a new class of laser-active materials, namely polycrystalls Nd:YAG, which is a promising candidate for the development of high-power lasers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
thermally induced birefingence in Nd-doped ceramic rods is a problem that can be solved.
, in spite of the high optical quality of the ceramics, the laser performance of the ceramic rods is limited by the thermally induced birerfingence.
, in spite of the high optical quality of the ceramics, the birefringent properties of the material are such that it cannot be used as a laser medium without additional treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the birefringent effect in ceramic rods can be neglected for laser applications.
the birefringent properties of ceramics can be controlled by thermal and/or stress loads.
the birefringent properties of Nd:YAG polycrystalls are determined by both the crystallographic and the thermal structure of the material.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is necessary to use a ceramic with a grain size of less than 10 micrometers to obtain a low level of beam modulation in a Nd:YAG rod.
it is necessary to take into account the depolarization in the analysis of laser systems using polycrystallyne Nd:YAG rods.
the phase delay of eigenpolarizations is not constant along the rod length.
